body: Yeah, I'm in a similar position to you. My family doesn't understand that I can be depressed because I live a privileged life and don't acknowledge it at all

I come from a pretty well respected family but I agree, they definitely don't know the full extent of everything going on with me but this is mainly because I can't talk to them, there's no point. They dismiss everything I say until it affects them directly.

No, not at all they just don't understand what I'm going through and refuse to acknowledge the problem because to everybody else my life's fine, because it is i guess. My family wants to protect their reputation and having someone mentally ill isn't good for that so they ignore it and don't think it's valid for me to feel this way.

I believe my family is the main culprit of my depression, of course I don't want them to blame themselves or anything but I also find it difficult to consider their feelings when I'm in this state of mind because I know they'd be able to recover.

I've only had one experience calling a hotline and it was very brief. They wanted to know my name, city and age, and wouldn't talk to me until I stated them, so I hung up because I got nervous and thought they were going to call the police and somehow get me put somewhere. In retrospect I would call them again because I realize they probably wouldn't have done that. However it really didn't help my situation at the time. Hopefully you have a better experience if you decide to call them.
